title: The Hodge conjecture for Fermat fourfolds: odd degrees up to 199 and the even-degree census to 250 — papers, exact certificates and verifiers
description:
Two companion manuscripts and the single self-verifying computational package they share.

The odd-degree note proves the Hodge conjecture for the Fermat fourfold X4m for every odd degree m ≤ 199, by three closure mechanisms — a *-split transport theorem, a two-pair standard closure, and a level-lifted closure of the exceptional degree-33 class — together with a complete computer-assisted census and its completeness proof. An exact Jacobi-sum computation at p = 67, carried out in Z[x]/Φ33 with no floating point, shows that no cycle defined over Q(ζ33) projects onto the exceptional block, and constrains the residue degrees of any field of definition.

The even-degree companion maps the even sector through degree 250: forty primitive classes survive the base predicates and the depth-2 closure oracle, deeper certificates close all but ten, an exchange theorem organises the residual into claim-equivalence walls, and two of them close — one by a coset transfer from an explicit *-split class, one by a 40-generator lattice certificate. Eight certified gap classes remain; they are not claimed to be non-algebraic.

The package. Three algorithmically independent census implementations; per-orbit witness certificates for all 78,299 orbit representatives across the 89 odd levels, with the terminal classes re-screened live rather than trusted from a label; per-level canonical SHA-256 hashes for both parities; exact Hermite-normal-form lattice tests with modular kernel witnesses for every non-membership and re-summed integer certificates for every membership; explicit machine-checkable routes for all thirty deep closures; and the sweeps behind the wall structure. One command runs every check with fresh-run semantics, and each verifier is tested to reject a deliberately corrupted certificate.
